meta.label: Mattresses
meta.attribution: Covers new mattresses sold in the United States. Every mattress sold in the US must meet the Consumer Product Safety Commission's flammability standard, 16 CFR Part 1633, but the standard sets a fire performance limit rather than naming a method: a brand can meet it with a chemical flame retardant treatment or with an inherently flame resistant fiber barrier such as wool or treated rayon, and is not required to say which one on the label. CertiPUR-US and GREENGUARD Gold, issued by UL Solutions, are the two most common independent finished-product certifications for foam content and chemical emissions in this category. GOTS and GOLS certify organic cotton, wool and latex from farm to finished product. All are paid, audited certification programs that a brand applies for, not a ranking service, and each brand's certificate can be checked independently: certipur.us/directory (whose listings are served from certifiedfoam.eandmonline.com) for CertiPUR-US, spot.ul.com for GREENGUARD, and the certified suppliers database at global-standards.org for GOTS. Recalls for breaking the federal flammability standard are published by the Consumer Product Safety Commission at cpsc.gov, and a recall of another model from the same brand is named in that brand's description and links rather than scored. Price is the brand's own listed price for a queen mattress in its base configuration, read directly on the brand's own site; queen prices for a given model move often with sales. A mattress with no named certification here is not necessarily unsafe, it means the page checked did not state one. Keeping a mattress that still supports you, rather than replacing it on a fixed schedule, remains the cheapest and lowest-impact option and is not scored as a product here. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Names what is excluded, not just a logo

products.name: Avocado Green Mattress
products.description: An organic latex and wool mattress carrying six simultaneous third-party certifications, more than any other brand in this list, backed by a 25-year warranty and a full year to decide. Its own site did not show a plain queen price without a promotional code at the time this was checked.

certification.note: Avocado's certifications page lists six finished-product certifications held at once: GOTS, OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Class I, MADE SAFE, EWG Verified, GREENGUARD Gold and UL Formaldehyde-Free Validation, and states GOTS certifies the finished product rather than a single component.

transparency.note: Avocado's certifications page explains that each of its six certifications 'tests for different substances, through different methodologies, against different exposure pathways', rather than treating one logo as covering everything.

durability.note: Avocado offers a 25-year limited warranty with full protection for the first ten years and prorated coverage after, plus a trial described as a full year to decide, with a 99 dollar return fee if returned after the first 30 days.

products.name: Naturepedic Verse
products.description: An organic mattress maker certified to the Global Organic Textile Standard since 2009, using GOTS-certified cotton and wool and GOLS-certified latex, with a 25-year warranty and a 100-night trial.

price.note: Naturepedic's Verse product page lists the queen size at 1,499 dollars.

certification.note: Naturepedic's certifications page says it has been GOTS certified since 2009, was the first MADE SAFE certified mattress brand in 2016 and the first FSC certified mattress brand in 2019, and lists GOLS, GREENGUARD Gold, UL Formaldehyde Free, Responsible Wool Standard and Responsible Down Standard among its certifications.

transparency.note: Naturepedic's certifications page states its entire manufacturing facility is GOTS certified, not just the products, and names each standard (GOTS, GOLS, FSC, EWG Verified, UL Non-Detectable PFAS) separately with the year it first achieved it.

durability.note: The Verse product page states a 25-year limited warranty and a 100-night, risk-free trial with a full refund if returned within that period.

products.name: Saatva Classic
products.description: A hybrid innerspring mattress combining CertiPUR-US certified foam with a GREENGUARD Gold certified flame barrier, sold direct with white-glove delivery, a lifetime warranty and a full year to return it.

price.note: The Saatva Classic product page lists the queen size at 2,229 dollars.

certification.note: The Saatva Classic product page states the mattress uses CertiPUR-US certified foams and is GREENGUARD Gold certified.

transparency.note: Saatva names both certifications on the product page itself and ties the GREENGUARD Gold claim specifically to the mattress's flame barrier component rather than the mattress as an undifferentiated whole.

durability.note: Saatva's warranty page describes a 'Friends for Life' lifetime warranty with full replacement at no charge for the first two years, and the Classic product page states a 365-night home trial.

products.name: Purple
products.description: The company behind the patented gel grid mattress. Its foam layers are CertiPUR-US certified, and it offers a 100-night trial and a 10-year warranty.

price.note: The Purple mattress page lists the queen size at 1,280 dollars, marked down from 1,599 dollars.

certification.note: Purple's mattress page states 'Purple only uses CertiPUR-US certified foam.'

transparency.note: Purple's mattress page states its CertiPUR-US claim in one line, 'Purple only uses CertiPUR-US certified foam', without naming which substances the certification excludes or mentioning the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

durability.note: Purple's mattress page offers a 100-night trial beginning at delivery and a warranty of up to 10 years from the date of original purchase.

products.name: Casper Original
products.description: One of the original bed-in-a-box brands. Its polyurethane foams are CertiPUR-US certified and made without ozone-depleting chemicals or the phthalates the Consumer Product Safety Commission regulates.

price.note: The Casper Original mattress page lists the queen size at a sale price of 1,295 dollars.

certification.note: The Casper Original product page states 'All of our polyurethane foams are CertiPUR-US certified.'

transparency.note: Casper's product page says its foams 'are made without ozone-depleting chemicals and phthalates regulated by the Consumer Product Safety Commission', naming the excluded categories rather than only the certification logo, though it does not address the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

products.name: Nectar Classic
products.description: A budget-friendly memory foam brand that markets its mattresses as fiberglass-free and CertiPUR-US certified, backed by a 365-night trial and a warranty it calls Forever.

price.note: The Nectar Classic mattress page lists the queen size at 699 dollars.

certification.note: Nectar's mattress page states the Classic is 'certified by CertiPUR-US to meet their standards for content, emissions, and durability.'

transparency.note: Nectar's page adds a specific fiberglass-free claim alongside the CertiPUR-US certification rather than stating the certification alone, though neither claim addresses the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

durability.note: Nectar's mattress page offers a 365-Night Home Trial, described as an entire year to decide, and a Forever Warranty.

products.name: Tuft & Needle Original
products.brand: foam, owned by Serta Simmons Bedding
products.description: A foam mattress brand certified to both CertiPUR-US and GREENGUARD Gold, with a 100-night trial and a 10-year warranty. Serta Simmons Bedding, which also owns Serta and Simmons Beautyrest, acquired it in 2018 and kept it operating as a separate brand.

price.note: The Tuft & Needle Original mattress page lists a regular price of 695 dollars.

certification.note: The Original mattress page states the foams were 'tested for and are free from harmful chemicals and harmful gasses' under CertiPUR-US, and separately states the mattress is GREENGUARD Gold certified, 'screened for over 10,000 harmful chemicals and VOCs.'

transparency.note: The Original mattress page states both certification names and what GREENGUARD Gold screens for, though it does not itemize the specific excluded chemicals the way Tempur-Pedic's or Simmons's pages do, or mention the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

durability.note: The Original mattress page states a 100-night sleep trial with a hassle-free return process and a 10-year limited warranty covering manufacturing and workmanship defects.

products.name: Sealy
products.description: One of the best-known mattress brands in the country, and part of the same parent company as Tempur-Pedic. Its own shop page lists several product lines from about 800 to 2,000 dollars for a queen and states no foam or emissions certification, but the CertiPUR-US directory lists Sealy and Sealy Posturepedic as participating brands.

price.note: Sealy's shop mattresses page lists queen starting prices of 799 dollars for Posturepedic Spring, 919 dollars for Cocoon by Sealy, 999 dollars for Posturepedic Hybrid and 1,999 dollars for Posturepedic Elite.

certification.note: Sealy's shop mattresses page, rechecked in October 2026, still states no CertiPUR-US, GREENGUARD or other third-party certification, but the certifier lists it: the CertiPUR-US directory has a brand-level listing for Sealy (www.sealy.com), a mattress manufacturer and retailer for adult, adjustable, custom and youth mattresses in the USA, valid through 2026, alongside a separate listing for Sealy Posturepedic. The listing covers the brand as a whole and does not name individual models, so the score sits at the low end of the range for CertiPUR-US alone.

transparency.note: The shop page names product lines and prices without describing materials, certifications or what a buyer's foam is made without. Every mattress sold in the US, including Sealy's, must still meet a separate mandatory flammability standard regardless of what this page states.

products.name: Serta Perfect Sleeper
products.description: A mainstream mattress brand whose foam is CertiPUR-US certified. It offers a 100-day in-home trial and a 10-year limited warranty.

price.note: The Serta Perfect Sleeper product page lists a price of 699 dollars.

certification.note: Serta's product page states 'CertiPUR-US Certified means our foam was tested for and is free from harmful chemicals and gasses.'

transparency.note: Serta's page repeats the CertiPUR-US claim in general terms without naming the specific excluded substances, and does not mention the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

durability.note: Serta's product page states purchases made directly from Serta.com are covered by a 100-Day In-Home Trial and a 10-year limited warranty covering manufacturing and workmanship defects.

products.name: Simmons Beautyrest Black
products.description: A mainstream innerspring and hybrid brand whose page names the specific substances its CertiPUR-US certified foam excludes: formaldehyde, flame retardants, restricted phthalates and heavy metals.

price.note: The Beautyrest Black mattress page lists a price of 1,749 dollars.

certification.note: The Beautyrest Black page states 'We use only CertiPUR-US certified foams in all of our products.'

transparency.note: The same page adds that the certified foams 'are made without formaldehyde, flame retardants, prohibited phthalates, and heavy metals, as well as meet low-VOC standards', naming the excluded categories rather than only the logo.

durability.note: The Beautyrest Black page offers a 100-Night In-Home Trial with a full refund if unhappy, and states 'we stand by our Beautyrest mattresses with a 10-Year Limited Warranty.'

products.name: Tempur-Pedic TEMPUR-Cloud
products.description: A premium memory foam brand whose CertiPUR-US certification page names the specific flame retardant chemicals, including the one known as Tris, that its foam is made without. Its current mattresses carry a 10-year warranty.

price.note: The TEMPUR-Cloud mattress page lists the queen size at 1,999 dollars.

certification.note: The TEMPUR-Cloud page states the performance foam is '100% CertiPUR-US certified' and made without ozone depleters, PBDE, TDCPP or TCEP flame retardants, formaldehyde, and mercury, lead or other heavy metals.

transparency.note: Tempur-Pedic's product page names the specific flame retardant chemicals it excludes, including the compound known as Tris, rather than stating the certification without detail.

durability.note: Tempur-Pedic's warranty page states a 10-Year Limited Warranty applies to mattresses purchased from October 1, 2022 onward; this page did not state a sleep trial length.

products.name: IKEA VALEVAG
products.description: IKEA's budget pocket-spring mattress. Its product page states it meets the mandatory durability standard EN 1957 and the mandatory US flammability standard 16 CFR 1633/1632, but does not name a voluntary foam or emissions certification.

price.note: IKEA's VALEVAG product page lists the queen size at 399 dollars.

certification.note: IKEA's VALEVAG page states the mattress 'has been tested and meets the requirements for durability set forth by standard EN 1957, and flammability requirements set forth by 16CFR 1633/1632', both mandatory safety standards rather than a voluntary chemical-emissions certification like CertiPUR-US or GREENGUARD Gold.

transparency.note: IKEA names the specific mandatory standards the mattress meets by number, which is more specific than a bare certification logo, though it names no voluntary chemical-content certification.

durability.note: IKEA's VALEVAG page offers a 10 year limited warranty and states 'Try at home for 90 days. Don't love it? Exchange it.'

products.name: Zinus Original Green Tea
products.description: A budget bed-in-a-box brand sold mostly online. Its foam is CertiPUR-US certified, and the company states it is made without phthalates, flame retardants or formaldehyde.

price.note: Zinus's Original Green Tea Memory Foam Mattress page lists the queen size at a sale price of 499 dollars, marked down from 718 dollars.

certification.note: Zinus's product page states 'CertiPUR-US certified foam is made without phthalates, flame retardants, formaldehyde, or harmful chemicals.'

transparency.note: Zinus names the specific excluded substances, phthalates, flame retardants and formaldehyde, in the same sentence as the certification claim rather than citing only the logo, though the page does not mention the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

durability.note: Zinus's product page states a 10 year limited warranty and a 100-day trial upon delivery with a refund if the customer is not satisfied.

products.name: Leesa Original
products.description: A direct-to-consumer brand using CertiPUR-US certified foam, with a 120-night trial and a limited lifetime warranty. Leesa says it has donated more than 43,000 mattresses to people in need since 2015.

price.note: Leesa's Original mattress page shows a queen listed at 999 dollars in its size comparison, marked down from 1,332 dollars.

certification.note: Leesa's Original mattress page states 'All foams are CertiPUR-US certified to meet their rigorous standards for emissions.'

transparency.note: Leesa's Original mattress page separately states the company has donated more than 43,000 mattresses to people in need since 2015, a specific, checkable claim rather than a vague giving statement, though the page does not mention the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must also meet.

durability.note: Leesa's Original mattress page lists a 120-night trial with free shipping and a limited lifetime warranty.

products.name: DreamCloud Classic Hybrid
products.description: A foam-and-coil hybrid at a low listed queen price, with CertiPUR-US certified foam, a fiberglass-free build, a 365-night trial and a warranty it describes as covering the mattress for life. It names no emissions certification beyond CertiPUR-US.

price.note: DreamCloud's Classic Hybrid page showed the queen at 699 dollars during a site-wide sale advertising up to 60 per cent off mattresses.

certification.note: The CertiPUR-US directory lists DreamCloud Sleep as a participating brand for adult mattresses, foam and pillows in the USA, valid through 2026, which matches the CertiPUR-US claim on DreamCloud's own product page.

transparency.note: DreamCloud's page states the Classic Hybrid is 100% fiberglass-free and certified by CertiPUR-US for content, emissions and durability, adding a specific fiberglass claim to the certification, but it does not list the excluded substances or mention the separate mandatory flammability standard every mattress must meet.

durability.note: DreamCloud's page offers a 365-Night Home Trial, described as a full year to decide, and a Forever Warranty it says 'ensures your mattress is covered for life'.

products.name: Awara Classic Hybrid
products.description: A latex, wool and coil hybrid that uses GOLS certified organic latex and FSC certified latex sourcing, with a fiberglass-free design, a 365-night trial and what it calls a Forever Warranty. It does not claim a whole-mattress organic certification or an emissions certification.

price.note: Awara's Classic Hybrid page showed the queen at 899 dollars during a sale advertising up to 50 per cent off mattresses.

certification.note: Awara's page describes GOLS and FSC certified organic latex and organic New Zealand wool, which certifies the latex component rather than the finished mattress; the page names no GOTS finished-product certification and no emissions certification such as GREENGUARD Gold.

transparency.note: Awara explains what the Global Organic Latex Standard requires and states the mattress has a fiberglass-free design, but it does not list other excluded substances or say how the mattress meets the mandatory flammability standard.

durability.note: Awara's page offers a 365-Night Home Trial and a Forever Warranty, with free shipping and returns.

products.name: Birch Natural
products.description: A latex, wool and coil hybrid with no polyurethane foam. Its latex is GOLS certified and the mattress is GREENGUARD Gold certified for low chemical emissions, backed by a 365-night trial and a limited lifetime warranty.

price.note: Birch's Natural mattress page lists the queen with standard breathable layers at 1,499 dollars, marked as 20 per cent off a reference price of 1,873.75 dollars.

certification.note: Birch's product page states its latex is Global Organic Latex Standard (GOLS) certified and that the mattress meets the chemical emissions requirements for GREENGUARD Gold certification; GOLS covers the latex rather than the whole mattress, and the page names no GOTS finished-product certificate.

transparency.note: The product page names what the mattress is made without, saying it is 'free of any polyurethane foams, fiberglass, formaldehyde, or pesticides', rather than relying on certification logos alone.

durability.note: Birch's warranty page states every Birch mattress is covered by a limited lifetime warranty against defects in workmanship and materials, and the product page offers a 365 Night Sleep Trial.

products.name: Brooklyn Bedding Signature Hybrid
products.description: A foam-and-coil hybrid assembled in the company's Arizona facility, with CertiPUR-US certified foam and a GREENGUARD Gold emissions certification, a 365-night trial and a limited lifetime warranty.

price.note: Brooklyn Bedding's Signature Hybrid page lists the queen at 1,465 dollars, with a site-wide 25 per cent promo code running at the time of the check.

certification.note: The Signature Hybrid page states 'Our mattresses are GREENGUARD Gold Certified and made with CertiPUR-US certified foams'.

transparency.note: The page names the excluded substances behind the claim, saying the mattresses are made without ozone depleters, PBDE flame retardants, mercury, lead, heavy metals and formaldehyde, though it does not say how the mattress meets the mandatory flammability standard.

durability.note: The Signature Hybrid page offers a 365-night trial that begins once the mattress is received, and a Limited Lifetime Warranty.

products.name: Bear Original
products.description: An all-foam mattress aimed at active sleepers, with CertiPUR-US certified foam and GREENGUARD Gold certification. Its page says it meets the federal flammability rules without fiberglass. Bear's warranty names Brooklyn Bedding as the manufacturer.

price.note: Bear's Original mattress page lists the queen in medium-firm at 998 dollars, with a 30 per cent promo code bringing it to 698.60 dollars at the time of the check.

certification.note: The Bear Original page states the mattress is GREENGUARD Gold certified and uses CertiPUR-US certified foam made without formaldehyde, ozone depleters, prohibited phthalates, and mercury, lead and other heavy metals.

transparency.note: Besides listing the excluded substances, the page says the mattress 'Meets strict fire safety standards (Federal Mattress Regulations 16 CFR 1633 and 1632) without the use of fiberglass fabric', one of the few pages checked that names the mandatory flammability rule and how it is met.

durability.note: Bear's warranty page states that mattresses bought from 1 February 2025 carry a limited lifetime warranty, and that it extends to mattresses manufactured by Brooklyn Bedding, LLC doing business as Bear Mattress; the product page offers a 365-night trial after a 30-night break-in period.

products.name: GhostBed Signature Foam
products.description: A memory foam mattress with CertiPUR-US certified foam, a 25-year limited warranty and a 101-night trial. In April 2024 the CPSC announced a recall of a different model, the GhostBed Natural, for failing the smoldering requirements of the federal mattress flammability rule; the remedy was a free compliant cover.

price.note: GhostBed's Signature Foam page lists the queen at 1,199 dollars against a stated comparison value of 2,866 dollars.

certification.note: The CertiPUR-US directory lists Ghostbed as a participating retailer for adult mattresses, toppers and pillows in Canada, the United Kingdom and the USA, valid through 2026, which matches the product page's statement that all GhostBed mattresses use CertiPUR-US certified foam.

transparency.note: The Signature Foam page lists what the certified foam is made without: ozone depleters, PBDE, TDCPP and TCEP flame retardants, mercury, lead and other heavy metals, formaldehyde, and phthalates regulated by the Consumer Product Safety Commission, plus low VOC emissions.

durability.note: The Signature Foam page states a 25-year limited warranty and a 101-night sleep trial with free returns; GhostBed's warranty page says its mattresses carry 10 to 25 year limited warranties depending on the model.

products.name: Happsy Organic Mattress
products.description: A certified organic latex, cotton, wool and coil mattress sold in a box at a mid-range price. It carries GOTS, GOLS, MADE SAFE, EWG Verified and GREENGUARD Gold, and says it passes the flammability rules without flame retardant chemicals or a flame barrier.

price.note: Happsy's product page lists the queen (SKU HPSY-Q) at 1,399 dollars, with a 20 per cent promo code running at the time of the check.

certification.note: The GOTS public database of certified suppliers lists HAPPSY, United States, for bedding and home textiles, confirming the company holds its own GOTS certification; Happsy's page lists GOTS, GOLS, MADE SAFE, EWG Verified and GREENGUARD Gold.

transparency.note: Happsy says its mattress 'does not contain any flame retardant chemicals or flame barriers of any kind while still passing all flammability requirements', names what it is made without (flame retardants, fiberglass, vinyl/PVC and polyurethane foam), and links the legally required law label for each size.

durability.note: Happsy's product page offers a 120-night risk-free trial with a full refund and a 20-year limited warranty.

products.name: Sleep On Latex Pure Green
products.description: An all-latex mattress with an organic cotton and wool cover, certified to GOTS, GOLS, Fair for Life fair trade and OEKO-TEX Standard 100, and listing each certificate number on its product page. It has a 10-year warranty and 100 days to return.

price.note: Sleep On Latex's Pure Green Natural Latex Mattress page lists the queen at 1,299 dollars.

certification.note: The GOTS public database lists Shevick Sales Corp DBA Sleep on Latex DBA Earthfoam, United States, for home textiles and undyed fabrics, confirming the GOTS certificate is held by the company itself; its product page also lists GOLS (CU 868773), Fair for Life and OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certificates.

transparency.note: The product page prints each certificate number next to its certifier, including GOTS-10236 from Oregon Tilth and CU868773 from Control Union, and states 'Every certification that we advertise is issued directly to our company.'

durability.note: The product page states each mattress 'comes with a comprehensive 10-year warranty' and that the mattress can be returned for free at any time within 100 days from delivery.

products.name: Nest Bedding Sparrow Signature Hybrid
products.description: A premium foam-and-coil hybrid, previously named the Alexander Signature Hybrid, with CertiPUR-US certified foam, a 365-night trial and a limited lifetime warranty. Its page lists each layer's foam density and firmness rating.

price.note: Nest Bedding's Sparrow Signature Hybrid page lists the queen at 2,229 dollars.

certification.note: The CertiPUR-US directory lists Nest Bedding as a participating brand and retailer for adult mattresses, youth mattresses and shredded foam pillows in the USA, valid through 2026, matching the Sparrow page's CertiPUR-US claim.

transparency.note: The Sparrow page lists every layer by thickness, foam density and firmness rating, for example '1.5 lb./30 ILD SmartFlow Support Foam', which is more specific than most pages checked, but it states the CertiPUR-US claim in general terms without naming excluded substances.

durability.note: Nest's warranty page, last reviewed January 2026, states a Limited Lifetime Warranty for qualifying manufacturing defects, with indentations over 1.5 inches eligible for review in years 1 to 5 and coverage judged case by case beyond 10 years; the Sparrow page offers a 365-night trial after a 30-night adjustment period.

products.name: Sleep Number ComfortMode
products.description: An air bed whose firmness each sleeper can adjust. It uses CertiPUR-US certified foam and offers a 100-night trial and a 10-year limited warranty, but names no emissions certification or excluded substances.

price.note: Sleep Number's ComfortMode page lists the queen at a sale price of 1,999 dollars for the mattress alone, without a base.

certification.note: The CertiPUR-US directory lists Sleep Number as a participating brand for adjustable mattresses, adult mattresses, toppers, pillows and RV mattresses in the USA, valid through 2026.

transparency.note: The ComfortMode page states that 'CertiPUR-US certified foams meet rigorous standards for content, emissions and durability' without naming the excluded substances, and does not mention the mandatory flammability standard.

durability.note: The ComfortMode page lists a 100-night trial and a 10-year limited warranty, and claims the bed is 'Designed to last 25 years', a claim footnoted as based on standard durability testing methods.

products.name: Amazon Basics Memory Foam
products.description: Amazon's own-brand memory foam mattress, the cheapest option here. It uses CertiPUR-US certified foam and an OEKO-TEX certified cover fabric, but has only a 1-year warranty. In July 2025 the CPSC announced a recall of about 2,700 of a different Amazon Basics model, the Premium Foam Eurotop, for violating the federal mattress flammability standard.

price.note: Amazon's listing for the Amazon Basics Soft Plush Feel Memory Foam Mattress, 10 inch, queen, showed 246.50 dollars, sold and shipped by Amazon.com, against a stated typical price of 271.93 dollars.

certification.note: The CertiPUR-US directory lists Amazon Basics as a participating brand for adult mattresses, toppers and pillows in the USA, valid through 2026.

transparency.note: The listing states 'CertiPUR-US Certified Foam and Oeko-Tex certified top fabric' and gives an OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification number, SHHO 060330, but names no excluded substances and does not mention the mandatory flammability standard.

durability.note: Amazon's Limited Warranty for Amazon Private Brands document, linked from the listing, gives Amazon Basics products a 1 year coverage period against defects in materials and workmanship; the listing offers a 90-day refund or replacement.

links.label: CPSC recall of Premium Foam Eurotop, 2025

products.name: PlushBeds Botanical Bliss
products.description: An all-latex mattress made in California with GOLS certified organic latex and GOTS certified organic cotton and wool. Its certificates are issued to its manufacturer, Sleep Technologies Inc., doing business as The Natural Latex Company. The GREENGUARD Gold emissions certificate it links expired on 3 October 2026, and the eco-INSTITUT certificate it links shows a validity of September 2022.

price.note: PlushBeds' Botanical Bliss page lists the queen, medium, 9 inch at 2,024 dollars.

certification.note: PlushBeds' certifications page links its certificates. The GREENGUARD Gold certificate it links, issued by UL for the Botanical Bliss, expired on 3 October 2026, ten days before this check, even though the page says the mattresses are GREENGUARD Gold 'tested and recertified every 90 days'; the linked eco-INSTITUT certificate, which covers the foam only, shows a validity of 09/2022. The 85 rests on what remains valid: a GOLS certificate from Control Union valid until 11 September 2027 and a GOTS scope certificate valid until 1 December 2026, both issued to Sleep Technologies Inc. dba The Natural Latex Company for bedding.

transparency.note: The GOTS public database lists Sleep Technologies Inc. dba The Natural Latex company, United States, for bedding and home textiles, the company named on the GOTS and GOLS certificates PlushBeds links, so a reader can check the claim against the certifier's own register.

durability.note: PlushBeds' warranty page states a Limited Lifetime warranty with repair or replacement for defects in the first ten years, then repair at a handling cost or replacement at a prorated charge starting at 50 per cent; its home page offers a 100-night risk-free trial.
